1983

When Cyndi Lauper's breakout hit "Girls Just Want to Have Fun" was released in 1983, it was accompanied by a music video that was a true community effort to create. Shot in the Lower East Side with borrowed video equipment and a largely volunteer cast, the music video cost less than $35,000 to make. Cameos include Cyndi's mother, her attorney, her manager David Wolf, her brother Butch, and professional wrestler "Captain" Lou Albano as Cyndi's father. 

The music video used a Quantel Mirage computer at Broadway Video to create special effects, the first time the system was used for a music video. Cyndi and her producer created several first-time-ever computer-generated images that mirrored the bubbly instrumentals of the song. The most iconic scene with this technique is Cyndi dancing with her strait-laced lawyer, leading the entire cast in a snake-dance through New York streets and ending up in Lauper's bedroom. 

The video began playing on MTV in October 1983 and would go on to win Best Female Video at the inaugural 1984 MTV Video Music Awards. The lasting love for "Girls Just Want to Have Fun" transcends its dance-able pop sound. Cyndi's personal doll appeared in the music video, seated atop a dresser in the shot of Cyndi's room. The doll is also pictured in a photoshoot and interview in the April 1984 issue of Life magazine titled "Cyndi Lauper Spies Success: Rock's Dizzy Diva".

The tablecloth appeared in the music video as the mother character, played by Cyndi's own mother Catrine Gallo, cracks eggs and frets over her daughter. In Cyndi's memoir, she recalls that the tablecloth came from Screaming Mimi's.

When Cyndi Lauper's solo studio album She's So Unusual was released October 14, 1983 by Portrait records, she was launched from relative obscurity to overnight stardom. She was nominated for five Grammys and would go on to win for Best New Artist and Best Album Package at the 27th Annual Grammy Awards. The success of the album placed Lauper as the first woman in history to have four top-five singles from a debut album and was one of the best-selling albums of the 1980s. In 2003, She's So Unusual was ranked at number 494 on Rolling Stone's list of the 500 greatest albums of all time, number 184 in a 2020 reboot of the list. In the mid-1980s, MTV collaborated with the WWF (now WWE) to intertwine mainstream popular culture and professional wrestling. The narrative began with Captain Lou Albano, a wrestling manager, appearing in Cyndi Lauper's 1983 music video for "Girls Just Want to Have Fun". A faux fight was created, and Lauper and Albano had a verbal brawl on WWF television programs. The scripted altercation led to Lauper choosing female wrestler Wendi Richter to represented her against Albano's The Fabulous Moolah in the 1984 "The Brawl to End It All" at Madison Square Garden, which was broadcast live on MTV.

In 1985, Hulk Hogan served as Lauper's bodyguard during her acceptance of her Grammy for Best New Artist. In the same year, Lauper appeared in Hogan's corner while he defended his WWF World Heavyweight Championship against "Rowdy" Roddy Piper during the 1985 "The War to Settle the Score" fight. The storyline eventually concluded with the first WrestleMania in 1985.

'Vive La Cocotte' Collection was a revolt against sloppy mediocrity of the mid-90s and a return to formality. The collection name is in reference to the 17th century French courtesan and author Ninon de l'Enclos -- Vive La Cocotte meaning 'long live the courtesan'. Corsets and bustles exaggerated the female figure, making the models appear like fashion illustrations. Westwood often commented that 'Vive La Cocotte' is her favorite collection.

'Les Femmes Ne Pas Toute Leur Coquetterie' Collection was the conclusion to previous iterations of these overtly feminine and exaggerated looks. This collection removed the stuffing and padding to relax the silhouettes.

Kinky Boots is a musical based on a 2005 British film by the same name written by Geoff Deane and Tim Firth and mostly inspired by true events. When Daryl Roth, a Tony Award-winning producer, the Kinky Boots film at the 2006 Sundance Film Festival, she felt that the story had the heart and soul to be a musical, and in 2010, a creative team was assembled with Harvey Fierstein, and Cyndi Lauper as the writer for the musical numbers. 

Following the story of Charlie Price, who inherits a shoe factory from his father in the north of England and forms a partnership with a cabaret performer and drag queen named Lola to produce a line of high-heeled boots to save the business. 

The original production of Kinky Boots premiered at the Bank of America Theatre in Chicago in October 2012, made its Broadway debut at the Al Hirschfeld Theatre in April 2013, and its West End debut in 2015. 

Kinky Boots was nominated for thirteen Tony nominations and won six, including Best Musical, Best Actor for Billy Porter and Best Score for Cyndi Lauper, her time as a Broadway songwriter. She is the first woman to win alone in that category. The musical's cast album premiered at number one on the Billboard Cast Albums chart and number fifty-one on the Billboard 200 chart. The show also won three Laurence Olivier Awards, including Best New Musical. 

Speaking to the success of the musical, Cyndi explained "It's a story about love and acceptance and friendship and overcoming obstacles and everyone can relate to that."
